operations.specification: Create a new guest account using device fingerprint for anonymous access. The service validates that the device fingerprint is unique (not already registered), creates a new guest record with current timestamp, generates JWT access and refresh tokens, creates an initial guest session record with connection metadata (IP, href, referrer), and returns the authorized response with tokens and guest information. The device fingerprint serves as the primary identification mechanism for guest users who haven't registered as members yet.
operations.description:
Register a new guest account for anonymous users accessing the todo application.

This endpoint creates a temporary guest identity using the device fingerprint as the unique identifier. Guest accounts allow unauthenticated users to explore the application and maintain session continuity without requiring email/password registration. The device fingerprint persists across sessions until the user either registers as a member or the guest account is cleaned up.

The operation validates that the provided device fingerprint is not already in use by checking the unique constraint on the device_fingerprint column in the todo_app_guests table. If the fingerprint already exists, the operation returns a conflict error. Upon successful validation, a new guest record is created with the current timestamp in the created_at field.

After creating the guest account, the service generates JWT access and refresh tokens for authentication. A guest session is also created in the todo_app_guest_sessions table to track the connection metadata including IP address, href, and referrer. The session includes an expiration timestamp for security lifecycle management.

This operation is the entry point for guest users. After joining, guests can use the returned access token to authenticate subsequent API requests. When the access token expires, guests can use the refresh token with the /auth/guest/refresh endpoint to obtain new tokens without re-joining.

requestBody.description: Guest registration information with device fingerprint for unique identification.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization tokens and account information after successful registration.

operations.specification: Refresh JWT tokens for an existing guest session. The service validates the provided refresh token against the guest's session in the todo_app_guest_sessions table, checks that the session has not expired by comparing expired_at with current timestamp, generates new access and refresh tokens, updates the session's expired_at timestamp to extend the session lifetime, and returns the new tokens. This allows guests to maintain continuous access without re-authenticating.
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens for an existing guest session.

This endpoint allows guest users to renew their access and refresh tokens without re-registering. When a guest's access token expires, they can use this endpoint with their valid refresh token to obtain new tokens and continue accessing the application seamlessly.

The operation validates the refresh token provided in the request body against the guest's session stored in the todo_app_guest_sessions table. The service checks that the session exists, belongs to the guest identified in the token, and has not expired by comparing the expired_at timestamp with the current time. If the session has expired or the refresh token is invalid, the operation returns an authentication error.

Upon successful validation, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated. The session's expired_at timestamp is updated to extend the session lifetime, allowing the guest to continue using the refresh token for future token renewals. This approach maintains security by limiting session duration while providing a smooth user experience.

Guests should call this endpoint before their access token expires to maintain uninterrupted access. If both the access token and refresh token expire, the guest must re-join using the /auth/guest/join endpoint with their device fingerprint.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for renewing guest session authentication.

responseBody.description: New authorization tokens for the refreshed guest session.

operations.description:
Creates a new member account in the todo application using email and password credentials.

This operation registers a new user by creating a record in the todo_app_members table with the provided email address and bcrypt-hashed password. The email must be unique across all member accounts. The display name is required for the user's profile.

Upon successful registration, the system generates JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication. The access token is used for subsequent API requests, while the refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

Additionally, an email verification record is created in the todo_app_member_email_verifications table with a unique token. This verification token should be sent to the user's email address to confirm their email ownership. The verification token has an expiration time for security purposes.

The operation returns the member's authorized session information including both tokens, allowing the user to immediately start using the application while email verification can be completed separately.

operations.description:
Authenticates a registered member using email and password credentials.

This operation validates the provided email address and password against the todo_app_members table. The password is verified using bcrypt comparison against the stored password_hash. If credentials are valid, a new session is created.

A session record is inserted into the todo_app_member_sessions table containing the JWT access token and refresh token. The session also captures connection metadata including the client IP address, the URL href where login was initiated, and the referrer URL for security auditing and session tracking.

The session has an expiration timestamp (expired_at) that determines when the tokens become invalid. Multiple sessions can exist for the same member across different devices or browsers.

Upon successful authentication, the operation returns the member's authorized session information with both access and refresh tokens, enabling the client to make authenticated API requests.

operations.description:
Renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This operation allows members to obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens when their current access token has expired or is about to expire. The refresh token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to ensure it exists and has not expired.

The service checks the expired_at timestamp in the session record to verify the refresh token is still valid. If the refresh token has expired, the operation fails and the user must re-authenticate by logging in again.

Upon successful validation, new access and refresh tokens are generated. The old session record may be updated with the new tokens or invalidated depending on the security policy (single-session vs multi-session support).

This operation enables seamless continued access to the application without requiring the user to re-enter credentials, while maintaining security through token expiration and rotation.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of active member sessions for the authenticated user.

This operation allows members to view their current login sessions across different devices and locations. Each session includes connection metadata such as IP address, initiation URL, referrer, and expiration time, enabling users to monitor account security and identify unauthorized access.

Sessions are filtered to only show those belonging to the authenticated member, ensuring complete data isolation. The endpoint supports pagination for users with many active sessions and provides sorting options by creation date or expiration time.

This operation is essential for security awareness, allowing users to review active sessions and identify any suspicious login activity. Combined with logout functionality, users can manage their session security effectively.

This operation allows authenticated members to view the details of a particular session, including connection metadata such as IP address, creation timestamp, and expiration time. The endpoint validates that the requesting user owns the session being queried. Users cannot access session information belonging to other users, enforcing complete data isolation between accounts as specified in the privacy requirements.

Session information includes connection details (IP, href, referrer) and temporal information (created_at, expired_at). Update the authenticated member's profile information in the todo_app_members table.

This operation allows members to modify their profile display name. The display name is shown in the user's profile and todo listings throughout the application. Members can update their display name at any time after account creation.

The operation requires active authentication and operates only on the authenticated member's own profile. Users cannot modify other members' profiles as the application maintains strict privacy boundaries between accounts. Only the display_name field is updated; email, password_hash, and other fields remain unchanged.

Validation rules enforce that the display name cannot be empty or contain only whitespace. The system rejects profile update requests that violate these constraints to maintain data quality.

Upon successful update, the operation returns the complete member profile with the updated display name and timestamps. The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect the modification time.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated member's profile in the todo_app_members table.

2. Validate display_name: must not be empty or whitespace-only
3. Update todo_app_members record where id equals authenticated member ID
4. Set updated_at timestamp to current time
5. Return updated member record with new display_name
6. Handle concurrency with optimistic locking if needed

Validation:
- display_name: required, non-empty string, trim whitespace before validation
- Reject if display_name is blank after trimming

- 400 if display_name validation fails

operations.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated member's profile information.

This operation returns the profile details of the currently logged-in member based on their active session. The response includes the member's display name, email address, and account timestamps. This endpoint is essential for profile viewing and account management features.

The operation requires an active authenticated session. The system automatically identifies the member from the session token and returns their profile data. Members cannot access other users' profiles as this is a private todo application with strict data isolation between accounts.

Profile information includes the display name which can be edited through the profile update endpoint, email address used for authentication, and account creation/update timestamps. Sensitive data like password hashes are never exposed in the response.

This endpoint is typically called when users navigate to their account settings or profile page to view their current information.
operations.name: at

Query the todo_app_members table for the authenticated member's profile.

1. Extract member ID from the authenticated session token
2. Query todo_app_members WHERE id = {memberId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Return profile fields: id, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at
4. Exclude password_hash from response for security
5. Handle case where member not found (session invalid or account deleted)
6. Ensure soft-deleted accounts cannot access this endpoint

Authentication: Requires valid member session token
Authorization: Member can only access their own profile
Error handling: Return 401 if not authenticated, 404 if account not found or deleted

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todo items owned by the authenticated member.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for managing personal todos. Users can filter their todo list by completion status (all, complete only, or incomplete only) and sort by creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order. The endpoint excludes soft-deleted todos that are in the trash.

The response includes pagination metadata enabling efficient navigation through large todo collections. Each todo item in the list displays essential information: title, completion status, optional start and due dates, and creation timestamp. Full todo details including descriptions are available through the detail retrieval endpoint.

All operations enforce strict ownership validation - users can only access todos they own. The system ensures complete data isolation between users, preventing any access to another user's todos through this or any other endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table filtering by todo_app_member_id from authenticated session. Apply completion status filter if provided (all, complete, or incomplete). Exclude soft-deleted todos (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results. Apply sorting based on requested field: created_at, started_at, or due_at with ascending or descending order. For started_at and due_at sorting, place null values at the end. Implement cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size. Join with todo_app_todo_edit_histories is not required for list view. Return paginated response with pagination metadata and todo summary data. Validate that user is authenticated as member before proceeding.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries with pagination metadata

requestBody.description: Search criteria including pagination, completion status filter, and sorting options

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific todo item from the todo_app_todos table by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete todo entity including all user-editable fields: title, optional description, optional start date (started_at), optional due date (due_at), completion status (completed), and audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at). The response provides all necessary data for displaying and managing an individual todo item in the user interface.

The endpoint enforces strict ownership validation through the todo_app_member_id foreign key relationship. Users can only access todos where the todo_app_member_id matches their authenticated member ID. If the requested todo does not exist or belongs to another user, the system returns a 404 Not Found response without revealing whether the todo exists. This security measure prevents unauthorized users from discovering information about other users' todos through existence checks, ensuring complete data isolation as required by the privacy requirements.

Only active (non-deleted) todos are accessible through this endpoint. Todos with a non-null deleted_at timestamp have been soft-deleted and moved to trash, and must be accessed through dedicated trash management endpoints instead. Attempting to retrieve a deleted todo through this endpoint will result in a 404 Not Found response.

This operation is typically used after retrieving a paginated todo list via PATCH /todoApp/member/todos, when a user selects a specific todo to view its full details or edit its properties. The returned data structure matches the ITodoAppTodo type with all fields populated according to the database schema. Related edit history can be retrieved separately via GET /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}/edit-histories.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the todo_app_todos table by the provided todoId UUID parameter. Before returning the todo, validate that the todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated member's ID from the session token. If the todo does not exist or belongs to a different member, return a 404 Not Found error to prevent information leakage about the existence of other users' todos. Ensure the todo is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) - deleted todos should not be accessible through this endpoint, only through trash-related endpoints. Return the complete todo entity including all fields: id, title, description, started_at, due_at, completed, created_at, and updated_at. Do not expose the todo_app_member_id or deleted_at fields in the response DTO as these are internal implementation details.

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated member.

This operation allows members to create a new todo with a required title and optional description, start date, and due date. The newly created todo is automatically marked as incomplete (completed=false) and associated with the authenticated member through the todo_app_member_id foreign key relationship.

The todo creation triggers automatic recording in the todo_app_todo_edit_histories table to maintain an audit trail of the initial creation. All field values are validated according to business rules: title must be provided, while description, started_at, and due_at can be null.

Created todos appear in the member's normal todo list and can be managed through other endpoints including GET /todos/{todoId} for detail viewing, PUT /todos/{todoId} for updates, and DELETE /todos/{todoId} for soft deletion to trash.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into todo_app_todos table with the following logic:

1. Extract authenticated member's ID from session context and set as todo_app_member_id
2. Validate that title is provided and not empty
3. Set completed=false by default for all new todos
4. Generate UUID for the id field
5. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
6. Set deleted_at=null (active todo)
7. Insert the new todo record
8. Create corresponding edit history entry in todo_app_todo_edit_histories table recording the initial field values
9. Return the complete created todo entity

Foreign key constraint ensures todo_app_member_id references valid todo_app_members.id. Cascade delete will remove todos if member is deleted.

responseBody.description: The created todo entity with all fields

requestBody.description: Todo creation data with required title and optional fields

operations.description:
Update an existing todo item's properties including title, description, start date, and due date.

This operation allows members to modify their own todo items by providing updated values for any combination of the editable fields. The title field is required and must be non-empty. Description, start date, and due date are optional and can be updated or cleared by setting them to null. Only the fields included in the request body will be modified; all other fields retain their current values.

The system enforces strict ownership validation - members can only update todos they own. Attempts to update another user's todo result in an access denied error. Additionally, todos that have been soft deleted (moved to trash) cannot be edited; such requests are rejected with an error indicating the todo is in trash.

Every successful update automatically creates a corresponding edit history record in the todo_app_todo_edit_histories table. This audit trail captures the timestamp of the change and the new values of all modified fields, enabling users to track the complete modification history of their todos.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time upon successful update. The response returns the complete updated todo entity with all fields including the new updated_at value.

Related operations:
- GET /todos/{todoId} - retrieve single todo details before editing
- PATCH /todos - list and search todos with filtering and pagination
- GET /todos/{todoId}/edit-histories - view the edit history audit trail
- PUT /todos/{todoId}/complete - toggle completion status separately
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table by todoId with ownership validation.

Implementation steps:
1. Retrieve todo from database by todoId
2. Validate todo exists - return 404 if not found
3. Validate ownership: todo.todo_app_member_id must match authenticated member's ID - return 403 if mismatch
4. Validate todo is not soft deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) - return 400 if in trash
5. Extract updatable fields from request body: title, description, started_at, due_at
6. Validate title is provided and non-empty (required field)
7. Update only the fields provided in request body, preserve other fields unchanged
8. Set updated_at to current timestamp
9. Wrap in database transaction:
   a. Update todo_app_todos record
   b. Create new todo_app_todo_edit_histories record capturing all field values after update
10. Return updated todo entity with all fields

Indexes utilized:
- Primary key lookup on id for fast retrieval

Edge cases:
- Concurrent updates: transaction ensures consistency
- Partial updates: only update fields present in request body
- Null values: description, started_at, due_at can be set to null explicitly
- Title cannot be empty or null

Authorization: member actor only, ownership required

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo by moving it to the trash.

This operation performs a soft deletion of the specified todo by setting its deleted_at timestamp. The todo is not permanently removed from the database but is instead moved to the trash, where it can be viewed, restored, or permanently deleted later.

Only the owner of the todo can delete it. The system validates ownership before proceeding with the deletion. Attempting to delete a todo that belongs to another user results in an access denied error.

After soft deletion, the todo no longer appears in the normal todo list but remains accessible through the trash endpoint. The edit history associated with the todo is retained along with the soft-deleted todo.

This operation is idempotent - deleting an already deleted todo will not cause an error. To permanently remove a todo and its edit history, use the permanent deletion endpoint from the trash.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete operation for todo_app_todos table implementing soft delete pattern.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate that the todoId exists in the database
2. Verify ownership by checking todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated member's ID
3. If todo is already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), the operation can still succeed (idempotent)
4. Set deleted_at to current timestamp
5. Update updated_at timestamp
6. Do NOT remove the record from the database
7. Do NOT delete associated edit history entries (they are deleted only on permanent deletion)

Database query:
UPDATE todo_app_todos
SET deleted_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE id = {todoId} AND todo_app_member_id = {authenticatedMemberId}

If no rows affected, either the todo doesn't exist or the member doesn't own it - return 404 or 403.

Edge cases:
- Todo already deleted: Still succeed (idempotent behavior)
- Todo doesn't exist: Return 404 Not Found
- Todo belongs to another user: Return 403 Forbidden
- Member not authenticated: Return 401 Unauthorized

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of edit history entries for a specific todo.

This operation provides access to the complete audit trail of changes made to a todo. Each edit history entry records the field values after an edit was made, including title, description, start date, due date, and completion status changes. Only fields that were actually modified in each edit contain values; unchanged fields are null.

Edit history entries are automatically created by the system whenever a todo is modified. Users cannot manually create, update, or delete individual history entries. The entries are immutable once created and provide a complete chronological record of all modifications.

Access is restricted to the todo owner only. Attempting to view edit history of a todo owned by another user results in an access denied error. If the todo has been permanently deleted, the edit history is also permanently deleted and this operation will fail.

Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order (most recent first) by default. The operation supports pagination to handle todos with extensive edit histories efficiently.

Apply pagination with cursor or offset-based approach.
Support sorting by created_at (ascending/descending).
Return edit history entries with all recorded field values (title, description, started_at, due_at, completed, created_at).
Handle case where todo has no edit history (return empty array with pagination metadata).
Reject requests if todo doesn't exist or belongs to another user.

Retrieve a specific edit history entry for a todo.

This operation returns detailed information about a single edit made to a todo, including the field values that were changed during that edit. The edit history entry shows what the title, description, start date, due date, and completion status were after the edit was made.

The endpoint validates that the todo belongs to the requesting user before returning the edit history. Users can only access edit histories for their own todos, ensuring complete privacy and data isolation. If the todo does not belong to the user, an access denied error is returned.

Each edit history entry records point-in-time snapshots of todo modifications. Fields that were not changed during a particular edit will be null in the history entry. The created_at field indicates when the edit was made.

This operation is typically used after retrieving the list of edit histories to examine a specific edit in detail. Edit histories are automatically created whenever a todo is edited and cannot be manually created or modified by users.

Query the todo_app_todo_edit_histories table by editHistoryId.

Return the complete edit history record including all fields: id, todo_app_todo_id, title, description, started_at, due_at, completed, and created_at.

Handle edge cases: Return 404 if the edit history entry does not exist or does not belong to the specified todo. Return 403 if the todo belongs to a different user.

Note: Edit histories are automatically created on todo edits and cannot be manually created, updated, or deleted by users.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of soft-deleted todos from the authenticated member's trash.

This endpoint provides access to todos that have been soft-deleted by the member. Soft-deleted todos have their deleted_at timestamp set and no longer appear in the normal todo list. Members can view these deleted todos in the trash to review, restore, or permanently delete them.

The operation supports filtering by completion status (completed or incomplete) and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date. When sorting by start date or due date, todos without those dates appear at the end of the list. Results are paginated to handle large numbers of deleted todos efficiently.

Only the authenticated member can access their own trash. The system enforces strict data isolation - members cannot view other users' deleted todos under any circumstances. This endpoint requires member authentication and will reject unauthenticated or guest requests.

Related operations: POST /todos/{todoId}/restore to restore a deleted todo, DELETE /todos/{todoId}/permanent to permanently delete from trash, PATCH /todos for viewing active todos.

Query todo_app_todos table with WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND todo_app_member_id = {authenticated_member_id}.

Apply pagination from request body (page, limit) with cursor-based or offset-based pagination.

Support filtering by completion status (completed field) if provided in request.

Support sorting by created_at, started_at, or due_at with ascending/descending order. Records with NULL started_at or due_at should appear at the end when sorting by those fields.

Join with todo_app_todo_edit_histories is NOT required for list view - only basic todo fields needed.

Ensure data isolation: only return todos belonging to the authenticated member.

operations.description:
Restore a soft-deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list.

This operation allows members to recover their deleted todos by clearing the soft-delete timestamp. When a todo is restored, it returns to the normal todo list with all its original properties intact including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and edit history. The creation date of the todo remains unchanged after restoration, maintaining the original creation timeline.

The operation validates that the todo exists, belongs to the authenticated member, and is currently in the trash (soft-deleted). If the todo is not deleted or belongs to another user, the request is rejected with an access denied error. Once restored, the todo behaves identically to todos that were never deleted and can be edited, completed, or deleted again.

This endpoint is part of the trash management workflow. Members typically use GET /todos/trash to view their deleted todos before deciding which ones to restore. For permanent removal instead of recovery, use DELETE /todos/trash/{todoId}.

Verify the todo is currently soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). If not deleted, reject the request as the todo is already active. Update the todo by setting deleted_at to NULL, effectively restoring it to active status. The todo's created_at timestamp remains unchanged per business requirements. Return the complete restored todo entity. Ensure transaction safety - if any validation fails, rollback without changes. Related operations: GET /todos/trash (list deleted todos), DELETE /todos/trash/{todoId} (permanent delete).

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash, removing it and all associated edit history records from the system.

This operation performs irreversible deletion of a soft-deleted todo that currently resides in the user's trash. The todo must have been previously soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) and must be owned by the authenticated member. Upon successful execution, the todo record is permanently removed from the todo_app_todos table, and all associated edit history entries in todo_app_todo_edit_histories are cascade-deleted.

This endpoint is specifically for permanent deletion from trash, distinct from the initial soft-delete operation that moves active todos to trash. Once this operation completes, the todo and its complete edit history cannot be recovered.

The operation validates that the todo exists, belongs to the authenticated member, and is currently in soft-deleted state. If any of these conditions fail, the request is rejected with an appropriate error response.

Related operations: PATCH /todos/trash for viewing trash contents, PATCH /todos/trash/{todoId}/restore for recovering deleted todos.

operations.specification:

ITodoAppTodoEditHistory.description: Complete edit history entry representing a point-in-time snapshot of changes made to a todo. This DTO captures what field values were after a specific edit operation. Fields that were not modified during the edit will be null, while changed fields contain their new values. The created_at timestamp indicates when the edit was made. Edit histories are automatically generated whenever a todo is edited and cannot be manually created or modified by users.
ITodoAppTodoEditHistory.x-autobe-specification: Direct query from todo_app_todo_edit_histories table by editHistoryId. All 8 fields map directly to DB columns: id, todo_app_todo_id, title, description, started_at, due_at, completed, created_at. Nullable fields (title, description, started_at, due_at, completed) return null when that field was not changed in this specific edit. Join with todo_app_todos on todo_app_todo_id to validate ownership (todo_app_member_id must match authenticated user's member ID). Return 404 if edit history not found or doesn't belong to specified todo. Return 403 if todo belongs to different user. Edit histories are append-only and automatically created on todo edits.
